questions.question: So if I buy the levis 501 shrink to fit will they get tighter after washing?

hybrid.answer:
**Yes. In his experience they shrink when they get wet, so he recommends buying them bigger.** In his most recent take (2025), The Iron Snail explains that the 501 Shrink-to-Fit is unsanforized denim: "you put it in the bathtub, it'll shrink," and you should usually go two sizes up [1].

**How much to size up**
- In 2021 he said Levi's recommends going two sizes bigger in the waist and two inches longer than you normally wear. He admitted it took him four pairs of 501s to accept that Levi's is right [2].
- If you try them on before getting them wet, he says they'll feel too big, but they come out right after the soak [3].
- In his 2023 comparison he followed this himself and bought size 32 STFs to compare with a size 30 rinsed pair [4].

**What happened when he didn't size up**
- His first pair was a 29 waist and 30 length. After soaking, the waist was very tight [5], but the length barely changed [6].
- A week later the waist and thighs had stretched enough that he could wear a belt comfortably [7].
- After a year he said that at first he could barely pull them on and couldn't breathe. Once broken in, though, they fit him really well, and he'd have bought a 32 length [8].

So the waist gets tight after the first soak and then loosens with wear. In his experience the length didn't shrink much.

**Washing tips**
How you wash them matters. He found that if you put STFs in the dryer they'd come out a lot smaller [9]. His advice is not to toss them in the dryer or rinse them in very hot water, which he says gives a really nice fit [10].

He doesn't say much about shrinkage on later washes; his comments are about the first soak and how the jeans stretch afterwards.

questions.question: So do you prefer [the Red Wing 3335s] over the 1907s?

hybrid.answer:
**Mostly yes, though by 2023 he'd softened on it and was getting rid of the 3335s.**

**Most recent (Sept 2023):** Culling his boot collection, he said he's on record calling the 3335s his favourite Red Wings of all time and that "they still might be", but he hedged that the 875s, the 1907s and the Iron Rangers "all have their own characteristics" that he really likes [1]. He still likes the 3335s because they're stitch-down, lighter and more nimble, and easier for walking or a light hike, but they were on the way out of his collection anyway [1].

**Original review (Oct 2022):** Here he was firm. He called the 3335s his favourite boots he'd ever had, saying they beat his Blundstones, the 1907s and the 875s [2]. His reasoning:

- **Use case:** heritage work boots are for heritage work, and he's mostly going on hikes and walking in the woods [2].
- **All-rounder:** he found them a "dramatically better all-around boot" [2], and he thinks they look "way cooler" [3].
- **Sole:** he preferred the Vibram mini lug, which he didn't expect to break down as fast as the crepe soles on the 875s and 1907s [4].

**Where the 1907 wins:** He said the 1907s and 875s are more beefily built, so if you need a tough boot the 3335s probably aren't the ones [2]. He also didn't think the 3335's stitch-down construction gives it much edge over a Goodyear-welted boot like the 1907, partly because it uses only a single stitch [5].

**Fit note:** He went true to size and they fit fine, but the slim, tapered shape squished his toes with wool socks [6].

questions.question: How does the made in England boot stack up to Solovairs? [Dr. Martens]

hybrid.answer:
**Short version:** The Iron Snail leans toward Solovair. In his only head-to-head take (2022), he called Solovair the better value: cheaper than Made in England Docs and, in his view, better built. The exception is if the Dr. Martens yellow stitching or the brand itself matters to you. [1][2]

**Where he thinks they're even (2022)**
- **Leather:** He said the Made in England leather is "probably on par" with Solovair's. [3]
- **Midsoles:** He put the better Made in England midsoles roughly on par with Solovair too. [3]

**Where he thinks Solovair wins (2022)**
- **Price:** Solovairs are cheaper than Made in England Docs. [2]
- **Shank:** Solovairs have a shank, which he says makes them more comfortable over long periods. Dr. Martens don't have one. [4][5]
- **Resoling:** He says they're Goodyear welted "in a more regularly accepted way," so they're easier to resole. [6]
- **Heritage:** Solovair is one of the original makers of Doc Martens. He says their 8-eye derby boot is "essentially the exact same boot." [4][6]
- **The catch:** Solovair doesn't do the yellow stitching. If that's a big deal, he says you'd have to go Made in England for the highest quality. Otherwise he "really suggest[s]" checking out Solovair. [1] He also said he wasn't sponsored by either brand. [7]

**Caveats on Solovair**
- In 2022 his own pair had a back tab rip off and a lace snap within eight wears. At the time he thought it was a manufacturing defect and expected them to fix it. [8]
- By September 2023 he said Solovair sent him the wrong things and told him to repair it himself. Despite that, he still "really like[s] these boots" and finds them comfortable. He'd only sell them to buy another pair of monkey boots. He did find the fit loose, which he put down to probably sizing wrong. [9][10]

**His later take on Made in England (2023)**
In a 2023 video he compared Made in England Docs only with the Made in Thailand ones, not with Solovair. His verdict was that the extra $90 is "probably not" worth it objectively. He sees them as for big Dr. Martens fans who want boots made the old way. [11][12]

He hasn't revisited the Solovair vs. Made in England comparison directly since 2022.

hybrid.answer:
In The Iron Snail's view, the main difference is the welt plus a few extras, and that makes the **1907 the better buy**. In his 2021 review he called it "the best Red Wing Moc Toe Boot in the business" [1].

**What sets them apart (2021 review)**
- **Construction:** The 875 is Goodyear welted. He calls Goodyear welts durable and pretty water resistant, and notes the space they leave lets Red Wing fill the boot with cork that molds to your foot [2]. The 1907 adds a storm welt, which he says is "invaluable" to him [3].
- **What the storm welt really is:** He's upfront that he isn't sure. The popular view he's seen on Reddit is that Red Wing simply stitches another strip of leather onto the welt [4]. He contrasts that with a true Norwegian welt, which he thinks folds the upper outward so water runs off "like a gutter" [5].
- **Price and extras:** The 1907 costs about $10 more than the 875 [6]. For that, you get Red Wing's removable leather footbed (normally about $40) and leather laces (normally about $15) [3]. He likes that you can pull the footbeds out at night so the boots dry faster [3]. He first said that's $55 of freebies, then corrected himself to "technically 45" since you paid the extra $10 [3].

**How waterproof is the 1907?**
In his standing-in-water test, the right boot leaked almost immediately through the stitching while the left stayed "dry as a bone" [7]. He called that a letdown, but he has "no doubt" they'd hold up fine in rain, grass or mud [7]. He didn't test the 875 this way.

**What they share (2022 update)**
By 2022, his favorite boot was neither one. It was the Red Wing 3335, which he says beats both the 1907 and the 875 [8]. One reason is that both moc toes use crepe soles, which he feels will break down faster than the 3335's Vibram mini lug sole [9]. He still says the 1907 and 875 are "more beefily constructed," so if you need a tough work boot, those are the better choice [8].

questions.question: How does Uniqlo compare to The Front General Store,  Proclub, and Hanes? ie what is the best budget shirt?

hybrid.answer:
**Short answer:** In his most recent t-shirt roundup, The Iron Snail calls **Uniqlo** the best budget shirt for the price. He treats **Front General Store** as the step-up pick if you want a Japan-made tee. He liked **Pro Club** and **Hanes** in 2024, but he hasn't put them head-to-head with Uniqlo, and later he flagged quality issues with cheap mass-market tees.

**Uniqlo: his budget benchmark**
- In his September 2025 roundup he says the $20 Uniqlo tee "is probably the best t-shirt that you can get bar none for the price" [1]. He notes it's open-end and "kind of rough" and calls it "your starter t-shirt" [2]. If you're taller or wider, he'd point you to Muji instead [3].
- In June 2025 he praised its bound neck collar, which "doesn't wiggle a lot" [4], and called the price-to-quality ratio "insane" [5].
- This has been consistent since July 2024, when he said the Uniqlo heavyweight crew neck "may be" the best bargain tee [6]. It shrank 2.3% in width and 2% in length [7].

**Front General Store: the upgrade**
- In 2025 he describes it as a $40, 100% made-in-Japan shirt with "great proportions, great feel" [8], and "still really good" [9].
- In 2024 he called it "one of the best shirts that you could possibly get" if you want a Japanese-made upgrade without spending over $40 [10]. He also said it might knock the most-voted shirt off the list [11]. He thinks it uses open-end yarn that has been sanded for softness [12]. He scored softness 6/10 and found almost no shrinkage because it's pre-washed [13].

**Pro Club (2024 only)**
- He'd never heard of it before viewers suggested it. He found it "the roughest shirt on this list" but liked everything about it, including the high neck with Lycra [14]. It scored softness 4/10 and shrank 6.86% in length [15].

**Hanes (Beefy-T, 2024)**
- He found it "much much softer than the Pro Club," and lighter [16], and called it "your classic $10 great shirt" [17]. It scored softness 7/10 but shrank 6.73% in length [18].
- By June 2025 he was more cautious about ultra-cheap mass-market tees from brands like Hanes and Gildan [19]. All five shirts he had from those brands had a defect [20].

**Bottom line by his reasoning:** Uniqlo is his pick for best budget shirt. Front General Store is worth it if you'll spend about $40 for Japan-made. Pro Club and Hanes are cheaper and he liked them, but both shrank a lot in length in his tests, and he hasn't directly ranked them against Uniqlo.

In the same 2025 videos, he also rated House of Blanks ($35, made in Canada) "an outstanding value" [21], and put Bronson and Bravestar "slightly above" Uniqlo on value [22].
